title: Ops, cost, migration & DR
oneLiner: CloudWatch watches, CloudTrail names who, Config checks rules. Compute Optimizer sizes, Cost Explorer recommends what to commit to. DMS moves data beyond databases. Pick the cheapest DR that meets RTO and RPO.

notes.text: Monitoring and governance: who answers what

head: Pillar
Ask
Typical answer
rows: Can we run and improve it?

questions.q: EC2 instances look over-provisioned. The team wants ML-based recommendations for a better instance type and size.

options.why: Right-sizing from utilization history is exactly its job.
Tells you what to commit to, not what size to run.
Alerts on spend; no sizing.
Quotas, not sizing.

questions.q: Steady EC2 usage has run for a year. Finance wants a recommendation on which Savings Plan to buy and how much to commit, with the least effort.

options.t: Use the Savings Plans purchase recommendations in Cost Explorer
options.why: Built from your usage history; you review and buy.
It right-sizes, it doesn't recommend pricing models.

options.t: No AWS tool helps; model it in a spreadsheet
options.why: Cost Explorer already does this.

options.t: Let Trusted Advisor auto-renew the plan
options.why: Trusted Advisor never buys or renews anything.

questions.q: Analysts need the most detailed billing data, per resource and per hour, queryable with SQL.

options.t: Cost and Usage Report (Data Exports) to S3, queried with Athena
options.why: The most granular billing data AWS gives.
Aggregated views, not raw line items.
Summaries against budgets.
API calls, not costs.

questions.q: A team wants an alert when forecasted monthly spend will pass $5,000, and to stop new instances if actual spend passes it.

options.t: AWS Budgets with a forecast alert and a budget action
options.why: Budgets alert on forecasts and can apply actions like an SCP or IAM policy.
Flags unusual spikes, not a fixed threshold.
Alerts on actual charges, no forecast, no actions.
Sizing.

questions.q: Which statement about AWS Trusted Advisor is correct today?

options.t: It has 6 categories, including operational excellence, and the full set of checks needs Business support or higher
options.why: Matches the current product.

options.t: It has 5 categories, and Basic support gets exactly 7 core checks
options.why: Outdated: 6 categories, and Basic gets more checks now.
It only alerts.

options.t: It replaces AWS Config for compliance rules
options.why: Different job: best-practice checks, not your own rules.

questions.q: Historical records in S3 must be streamed into Kinesis Data Streams for a new consumer, with no custom code.

options.t: AWS DMS with S3 as the source and Kinesis Data Streams as the target
options.why: Both are valid DMS endpoints, so it's configuration only.

options.t: A Lambda function that reads S3 and calls PutRecords
options.why: Works, but it's custom code.

options.t: Firehose from S3 to Kinesis Data Streams
options.why: Firehose delivers to destinations; S3 isn't a Firehose source and KDS isn't a target.

options.t: DMS only moves databases, so use DataSync
options.why: DataSync copies files between storage, not into streams.

questions.q: An on-prem Oracle database must continuously replicate into Amazon Redshift for analytics with the least development time and no servers to manage.

options.t: DMS (serverless) with full load + CDC, using SCT to convert the schema
options.why: Managed replication with ongoing change capture.

options.t: Nightly exports to S3 and COPY into Redshift
options.why: Not continuous, and scripts to maintain.
Batch ETL, more to build.
Offline, one-off transfers.

questions.q: A company moves from SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with stored procedures. Which pair of tools fits?

options.t: Schema conversion (SCT or DMS Schema Conversion) plus DMS for the data
options.why: Different engines need the schema and code converted first.
Moves data, doesn't convert stored procedures.

options.t: A native snapshot restore into Aurora
options.why: Snapshots only restore to the same engine family.
Rehosts servers, doesn't convert databases.

questions.q: RDS MySQL must move to Aurora MySQL with the least effort.

options.t: Restore an RDS MySQL snapshot into an Aurora MySQL cluster (or create an Aurora read replica and promote it)
options.why: Same engine, so no DMS or schema conversion.
SCT is for different engines.

options.t: Export to CSV and load into Aurora
options.why: Slow and manual.
For servers, not managed databases.

questions.q: 200 on-prem VMs must move to EC2 quickly with minimal changes and a short cutover.

options.why: Replicates disks continuously and launches EC2 at cutover.
Moves files, not whole servers.
Databases only.
A rebuild, not a rehost.

questions.q: A non-critical internal app can be down for a day and lose a few hours of data. What's the most cost-effective DR?

options.t: Backup and restore to another region
options.why: Nothing runs in DR, so it's cheapest; RTO/RPO in hours fits.
Costs more for a faster recovery nobody needs.
Runs a whole scaled-down stack.
The most expensive option.

questions.q: DR must recover in about 30 minutes with minutes of data loss. The database should replicate continuously, but app servers shouldn't run until needed.

options.why: Data replicated and running; compute starts from AMIs at failover.
Hours to restore.
Keeps servers running, which the brief rules out.
Full production running in both.

questions.q: A business-critical app needs recovery in minutes. Budget allows a scaled-down but fully working copy in another region.

options.why: A small full stack that scales up on failover.
Servers off, so recovery takes longer.
Hours.
Full size in both regions; more than the budget allows.

questions.q: On-prem servers need DR on AWS with RPO in seconds and RTO in minutes, without paying for running servers until a disaster.

options.why: Continuous block replication to cheap staging; launches instances on failover.
RPO up to a day.

options.t: A warm standby fleet on EC2
options.why: Pays for running servers all the time.
Offline transfer.

questions.q: Backups for EC2, RDS and DynamoDB must be managed centrally and no one, not even root, may delete them during retention.

options.t: AWS Backup plans with Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode
options.why: Central policies plus WORM vaults.

options.t: Per-service snapshots with IAM deny policies
options.why: Root and admins can change IAM.

options.t: S3 Versioning on a bucket of exports
options.why: Doesn't cover those services' native backups.
EBS snapshots and AMIs only.

questions.q: A security group was deleted last night. Who did it?

options.why: Records every API call with the caller.
Shows the resource changed, but CloudTrail names the caller.
Performance, not actions.
Network traffic, not API calls.

questions.q: Any EBS volume created unencrypted must be flagged and fixed automatically with the least custom code.

options.t: An AWS Config managed rule with SSM Automation remediation
options.why: Detects and fixes using built-in pieces.

options.t: CloudTrail with a Lambda that scans logs
options.why: Custom code.
Custom and delayed.
Best-practice checks, no custom remediation.

questions.q: A Lambda function must run whenever an EC2 instance enters the stopped state.

options.t: An EventBridge rule on EC2 state-change events targeting the Lambda
options.why: Native event, no polling.
Indirect and unreliable.
Detects unusual API volume, not state changes.

options.t: A cron Lambda that lists instances every minute
options.why: Polling.

questions.q: Ops needs memory utilization for EC2 instances in CloudWatch.

options.t: Install the CloudWatch agent on the instances
options.why: Memory is inside the OS; the hypervisor can't see it.
Adds 1-minute metrics, still no memory.
Network data.
API calls.

questions.q: Admins need shell access to instances in private subnets, with no open inbound ports, no bastion, and every session logged.

options.why: Agent-based access over HTTPS with logging.

options.t: A bastion host in a public subnet
options.why: Opens port 22 and is one more server.

options.t: EC2 Instance Connect with public IPs
options.why: Needs inbound SSH and public exposure.
Ports and keys still to manage.
